schedule.topic: EXAM REVIEW
FINAL EXAM (40%)

Contracts: an introduction. Formation of contract: elements of a legally enforceable contract (intention, offer, acceptance, consideration). Cases: Balfour v Balfour; Jones v Padavatton; Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball; St John Tugboat v Irving Refinery
Formation of a contract (cont'd): consideration; gratuitous promises; estoppel; form and writing. Cases: Central London Property Trust v High Trees House; Sargent v Nicholson
Formation of contract: legality; Statute of Frauds; capacity; minors; incompetence. Cases: Nash v Inman; Toronto Marlboro Major Junior A Hockey Club v Tonelli

MIDTERM TEST #1 (30%), chapters 9-12, during in-person class. Then contract interpretation: classification of contractual provisions (terms, representations, warranties and conditions); parole evidence rule; penalty clauses; privity; vicarious performance; assignment; discharge. Cases: Tilden Rent-a-Car v Clendenning; Hirsch v duBrule; Krell v Henry; Taylor v Caldwell
schedule.due_item: MIDTERM TEST #1 (30%); Chapters 9-12; During in person class

schedule.topic: Discharge and frustration. Cases: Taylor v Caldwell

Breach of contract; remedies; damages; mitigation. Cases: Baxendale [Hadley v Baxendale]; Jarvis v Swans Tours
Study Week
Study Week

Midterm Test #2 (30%), chapters 11-15 and 17. Then introduction to tort law: history; types; elements; levels of guilty mentality. Intentional torts: assault; battery; intentional infliction of mental suffering; false imprisonment; malicious prosecution; abuse of process; trespass to land; nuisance; trespass to chattels; privacy; intrusion upon seclusion. Cases: Malette v Shulman; Prinzo v Baycrest; Wilkinson v Downton; Banyasz v K-Mart; Nelles v Ontario; Jones v Tsige; Hill v Church of Scientology

Intentional torts (continued). Defences to intentional torts: consent; self-defence; defence of others; defence of property; provocation; necessity; legal authority; limitation periods; defences to defamation; anti-SLAPP legislation
Introduction to negligence: elements; damages. Cases: Donoghue v Stevenson; Mustapha v Culligan Waters; Palsgraf v Long Island Railway; Crocker v Sundance; Snushall v Fulsang
Defences to negligence: voluntary assumption of risk; contributory negligence; limitation periods; illegality; multiple tortfeasors (apportionment). Cases: Crocker v Sundance; Snushall v Fulsang

Special cases of liability: occupiers liability; host liability; product liability; strict liability; vicarious liability; limitations. Cases: Rylands v Fletcher; Resurfice Corp v Hanke; Jordan House v Menow; Hunt v Sutton House Realty; Childs v Desormeaux; Rankin v JJ
Remedies: purpose; types. Cases: Andrews v Grand and Toy; Arnold v Teno; Thornton v Prince George School. FINAL EXAM in last in-person class: chapters 1-8 (40%)
